speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I’m Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if you have experienced any recent fever, sore throat, or joint pain before these blisters and ulcers appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any similar lesions or blistering on your trunk, back, or scalp, and have you noticed any skin sloughing or positive Nikolsky sign?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the blisters on your forearm tense and intact, or do they rupture easily to leave crusted erosions? Also, are the mouth ulcers painful and located on the gums or inside the cheeks?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, osteoarthritis. Social history: Has started hiking in the woods on weekends. No relevant travel history.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient reports that the blisters on her forearm are tense and intact, while the mouth ulcers are painful and located on the gums and inside of her cheeks. She also notes that the blisters do not rupture easily.

speaker: Patient
text: No recent illnesses, denies fever, respiratory symptoms, or gastrointestinal symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your family history of autoimmune conditions and the presence of tense blisters with painful mucosal involvement, I suspect an autoimmune blistering disease. REQUEST TEST: Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin.
